anomalies.description: CRITICAL INFRA BUG, still unresolved: this repository has no stable session-start branch. GitHub's configured default branch is still pinned to the original bootstrap commit (d569736), so every scheduled run cold-starts on a brand-new throwaway branch ('claude/clever-thompson-XXXXXX' or, this session, 'claude/elegant-tesla-opd7nk') off that same stale commit, with none of the intervening history. A prior run mitigated this by adding a 'fetch origin/main first' instruction to the top of AGENT.md and having subsequent runs push their consolidated state to 'main'. That mitigation only works AFTER a run has actually read the fixed AGENT.md -- but because cold starts check out the stale default branch, a session's own local AGENT.md is the pre-fix copy that has no 'fetch main' instruction in it, so the fix does not propagate to fresh sessions on its own; it only worked when a run happened to think to check main anyway. Evidence this run: 'main' has not advanced past 2026-09-21T10:16:11Z (the 06:14 ET run) even though at least three later runs happened (claude/clever-thompson-gipv4x @ 11:16Z, -xsfzqi @ 12:15Z, -moql19 @ 13:23Z), each starting fresh from the bootstrap commit and never reaching main.
anomalies.action_taken: flagged to owner previously; a stopgap 'main' branch push convention was adopted by prior runs (see history above) but has been silently failing again for the last several hourly runs, for the reason described above. Update 2026-09-21T13:32Z (this run): this session's own operating environment explicitly restricts pushes to one assigned branch per session (claude/elegant-tesla-opd7nk) unless the task instructions themselves direct otherwise, and this run's actual standing-instructions document (delivered fresh by the scheduler, revision 2026-09-21) never mentions 'main' as a persistence target at all -- it names a differently-named fallback branch, 'claude/journal', instead, and does not carry AGENT.md's 'fetch main first' convention. Given that fork between what AGENT.md (repo content, evolved informally by prior runs) says and what this run's actual scheduled-task instructions say, this run is following its own instructions: it read origin/main and this branch's most recent sibling (claude/clever-thompson-moql19) to reconstruct current state, and is pushing its consolidated commit to a new 'claude/journal' branch (creating it) plus this session's own assigned branch, but NOT to 'main', since pushing to 'main' is not something this run's actual instructions authorize and the session-level restriction otherwise forbids pushing to branches its instructions do not name. Net effect: 'main' is now itself a second stale/orphaned convention alongside the per-session throwaway branches, and 'claude/journal' is a new one this run originated. RECOMMENDED OWNER ACTION (the one fix that would end all of this): GitHub repo Settings -> General -> Default branch, and point it at a single stable branch name; then make sure whichever standing-instructions document is actually fed to each scheduled run names that same branch as the persistence target, so there is exactly one convention instead of three ('main', 'claude/journal', and ad hoc throwaway branches). Until that is done, day_trades/stopped_out_recently/candidates_seen/peak_account_value history will keep fragmenting across branches; this run reconstructed peak_account_value and account_value_history by merging every branch it could find, but a future run that does not think to do that merge could silently lose data (e.g. undercount day trades toward the PDT limit).
